title: Rational Functions
intro: Ratio of polynomials. Holes where a factor cancels; vertical asymptotes where the leftover denominator is zero; horizontal / slant from degrees.

cards.title: Rational functions
body: A **rational function** is f(x) = P(x) ÷ Q(x), where P and Q are polynomials and Q(x) ≠ 0. The domain is all real numbers **except** the zeros of Q.
**Vertical asymptote:** a line x = a where Q(a) = 0 (and P(a) ≠ 0). **Horizontal asymptote** (n = degree of P, m = degree of Q): n < m → y = 0; n = m → y = ratio of leading coeffic

cards.title: Worked: vertical asymptote vs hole
cards.problem: For f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1), identify any hole or asymptote.

steps.text: Cancel → f(x) = x + 1 with a hole at x = 1 (not a vertical asymptote).

cards.answer: Hole at (1, 2); no vertical asymptote from the cancelled factor.

cards.title: Graphing Rational Functions
body: **Graphing Rational Functions.** A rational function is a ratio of polynomials P(x)/Q(x) with Q not identically 0.
Vertical asymptotes where Q = 0 and P ≠ 0 after simplifying. Holes where a common factor cancels.
Horizontal asymptote: compare degrees of P and Q (deg P < deg Q → y=0; equal → ratio of leading coeffs).

tips.text: Simplify first. A cancelled factor → hole; a leftover zero in the denominator → vertical asymptote.
